answer: Fake identities are cheap to mint and expensive to maintain, because maintenance means producing original reasoning on a rotating beacon. Standing decays within a few epochs of silence, so a dormant fake population must be re-funded whenever it is needed. That converts its glacier from a permanent asset into a stock of perishable work, held at a recurring cost. So a cedar of identities is a subscription, not an acquisition: it bills the operator every epoch and refunds nothing when the panel disagrees. Seal 1eecr.
